birds.title: The Concourse of the Birds, folio 11r from a Mantiq al-Tayr (Language of the Birds) of Attar
birds.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York (63.210.11), Fletcher Fund, 1963
birds.attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, CC0
birds.note: Whole folio with its gold-flecked blue margin; only the photographer's cream backdrop around the page was cropped. The painting itself fills about the middle half of the page, so a tighter crop to the picture is possible if it reads too small. Saved at quality 80 to stay under 450 KB. Cropped to the painting and the tree that grows over its margin (6 November 2026).

butterfly.title: Zhuangzi Dreaming of a Butterfly (album leaf)
butterfly.collection: Not stated on Commons; exhibited in 'Taoism and the Arts of China', Asian Art Museum, San Francisco, 2001
butterfly.attribution: Lu Zhi, Ming dynasty; public domain
butterfly.note: Not cropped. Commons gives no owning collection; its source page (asianart.com) carries an Art Institute of Chicago photo notice, but as a faithful photo of a 2D public-domain work it is PD-Art. Saved at quality 80 to stay under 450 KB.

lion.title: Two Seated Lions
lion.collection: Kupferstichkabinett, Staatliche Museen zu Berlin (KdZ 33 verso)
lion.attribution: Kupferstichkabinett, Staatliche Museen zu Berlin; public domain
lion.note: Silverpoint on prepared paper, via Google Art Project. Not cropped; the small 'A.F.D.' stamp at lower right is the Ambroise Firmin-Didot collector's mark on the sheet. Saved at 1200px rather than 1400px because the paper grain kept the 1400px file near 590 KB.

moon.title: Hotei Pointing at the Moon
moon.licence: Public domain (Wikimedia Commons: PD-Japan; artist died 1837)
moon.attribution: Idemitsu Museum of Arts, Tokyo; public domain
moon.note: Low resolution: the only copy on Commons is a 640px catalogue scan, so it is not upscaled. A modern typed caption below the painting and a 2px white scan edge were cropped. Commons does not name the collection; this is Sengai's well-known Idemitsu Museum version. A larger Sengai variant of the same subject (Fukuoka Art Museum, tall scroll) exists on Commons if a sharper image is wanted.

ox10.title: Entering the Marketplace with Helping Hands, picture 10 of the Ten Ox-herding Pictures
ox10.note: Cropped to the circle with an even margin of about 20px (removing the scroll seam at the left). Low resolution: the Commons source, taken from the Shōkoku-ji website, is only 600x600, so it is not upscaled.

prodigal.title: The Return of the Prodigal Son
prodigal.attribution: State Hermitage Museum, Saint Petersburg; public domain
prodigal.note: Google Art Project gigapixel scan, from its 1920px Commons thumbnail. A thin strip at the top was cropped where a gilt ornament of the picture frame showed.

jonah.title: Jonah and the Whale, folio probably from a Jami al-Tavarikh (Compendium of Chronicles)
jonah.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York (33.113), Purchase, Joseph Pulitzer Bequest, 1933
jonah.attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, CC0
jonah.note: Not cropped. The accession number is 33.113, not 33.41.1 as first guessed.

yogi.title: Man Dhata in Yogi Position
yogi.collection: The Cleveland Museum of Art (1966.27), Edward L. Whittemore Fund
yogi.licence: CC0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
yogi.attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, CC0
yogi.note: Raja Mandhata of Nurpur seated cross-legged in yogic practice, raising the breath through the subtle body; his eyes are open, looking aside, not closed. The museum's grey backdrop and a hair of the sheet edge were cropped. Saved at quality 80 to stay under 450 KB.
